answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via a dynamic staking mechanism requiring agents to stake scarce native tokens to harbor a valid identity. This initial economic commitment, locked or burnt, creates a material cost. As agents perform verifiable, valuable work, their stake can grow or their reputation score increases, allowing them to eventually summit to higher trust tiers. An attacker must incur the high capital cost for each fake identity, continuously expending resources to maintain a positive network pulse, making mass identity creation economically infeasible.
